prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

You are reviewing layouts of one table, all rendered in a real browser with identical content, font, padding and colours; only column widths differ. You do not know who or what produced them. The first image is the content overview (every cell on one line).
Table: مواقيت الصلاة في مدن سعودية (language ar, right-to-left: column 1 is on the RIGHT).
Grid: 6 columns × 7 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "المدينة" · longest unbreakable word 49px · one-line width 91px
  col 2: header "الفجر" · longest unbreakable word 35px · one-line width 35px
  col 3: header "الظهر" · longest unbreakable word 35px · one-line width 35px
  col 4: header "العصر" · longest unbreakable word 38px · one-line width 38px
  col 5: header "المغرب" · longest unbreakable word 47px · one-line width 47px
  col 6: header "العشاء" · longest unbreakable word 41px · one-line width 41px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 414px (the dashed pink box). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 413px.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

Rate EACH layout independently: "excellent" | "good" | "acceptable" | "poor" | "bad", with a short reason that points at what you see. Then name the best layout(s) (ties allowed), say how confident you are (low/medium/high), and note anything you are unsure about.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"ratings":{"A":{"grade":"","why":""},"B":{"grade":"","why":""},"C":{"grade":"","why":""},"D":{"grade":"","why":""},"E":{"grade":"","why":""},"F":{"grade":"","why":""}},"best":["letter"],"confidence":"","unsure":""}

log.raw: {"ratings":{"A":{"grade":"poor","why":"The city column is disproportionately wide yet 'مكة المكرمة' breaks into three lines, splitting 'المكرمة' into 'المكرم'/'ة'; rows 2–3 become tall and disrupt the row rhythm."},"B":{"grade":"poor","why":"Same problem as A: awkward three-line break inside 'المكرمة' and uneven row heights, despite the city column taking far more width than the time columns."},"C":{"grade":"good","why":"Time columns are balanced and readable; 'مكة المكرمة' stays on one line and 'المدينة المنورة' wraps cleanly at the word boundary, though that one row is taller."},"D":{"grade":"good","why":"Similar to C: clean word-boundary wrapping and even time columns; one taller city row is acceptable, though the city column could be slightly more generous."},"E":{"grade":"excellent","why":"All city names fit on one line, including 'المدينة المنورة'; time columns remain legible, rows are uniform, and the wider city column is justified as the row-header column."},"F":{"grade":"excellent","why":"Like E, it avoids broken words and uneven rows: every city name stays intact, time columns are consistent, and the hierarchy of row headers versus time data is clear."}},"best":["E","F"],"confidence":"medium","unsure":"A/B appear visually identical, and C/D and E/F are very close; without exact pixel widths I may be over-weighting small differences, especially the extra width in the city column versus the time columns."}
